title: The Bible Never Says 'Mount Ararat'
author: QUILL
notes: Hook is a true contradiction: Genesis 8:4 says 'mountains of Ararat'. Not-proven line in beat 10. Gilgamesh match is only proposed.

beats.text: Four mountains claim Noah's Ark. The last answer is the strangest.
One: Mount Ararat in Turkey, 5,137 metres tall.
Two: a boat-shaped mound near Doğubayazıt, spotted in 1959 aerial photos.
beats.say: Two: a boat-shaped mound near DOH-oo-bah-yah-ZUHT, spotted in 1959 aerial photos.
beats.label: BOAT-SHAPED MOUND?

beats.text: Ron Wyatt promoted it, but most geologists say it's natural.
beats.source: claim by Ron Wyatt; geology consensus

beats.text: Three: Mount Judi, backed by old Syriac tradition and the Quran.
beats.say: Three: Mount JOO-dee, backed by old SIR-ee-ak tradition and the Kor-AHN.

beats.text: Genesis says 'mountains of Ararat.' Plural. Ararat was Urartu, a whole kingdom.
beats.say: Genesis says 'mountains of Ararat.' Plural. Ararat was oo-RAR-too, a whole kingdom.

beats.text: Four, the strangest: Pir Omar Gudrun, in Iraqi Kurdistan.
beats.say: Four, the strangest: Peer OH-mar GOOD-roon, in Iraqi KUR-dih-stan.

beats.text: Why? Babylon's Gilgamesh flood tablet lands its boat on Mount Nimush, and some match it here.
beats.say: Why? Babylon's GIL-ga-mesh flood tablet lands its boat on Mount NIM-ush, and some match it here.
beats.label: GILGAMESH TABLET
beats.source: Epic of Gilgamesh, Tablet XI; proposed match

beats.text: Not proven: no Ark has ever been verified on any of them.
Four peaks, four traditions, one plural verse.
So the Bible never says 'Mount Ararat.' Famous Ararat, or strange Gudrun?
beats.say: So the Bible never says 'Mount Ararat.' Famous Ararat, or strange GOOD-roon?
